draftBefore.emotion: a factual, neutral observation of a day that has already passed
notes: While 'kinou' is the most common way to say yesterday, you may sometimes hear 'sakujitsu' in more formal or written contexts.
Unlike English, which uses 'yesterday' as both an adverb and a noun, 'kinou' behaves primarily like a time-indicating adverb in Japanese sentences.

faults.quote: Unlike English, which uses 'yesterday' as both an adverb and a noun
faults.why: False claim; 昨日 (kinō) is both a temporal noun (taking は, の, etc.) and an adverb in Japanese.
